title: Every governed path gets its denyWrite entry, with no exemption for .claude/** or .mcp.json

context.task: Close the hole a review found on 2026-10-14: Bash can write .claude/memory/, a governed path, because the sandbox's denyWrite exempts .claude/** and .mcp.json on the belief that Claude Code protects them by itself. It protects only part of .claude. AGENTS 7.3 requires every governed path to have its denyWrite entry.

problem: On 2026-10-14 a probe inside this session's sandbox opened .claude/memory/MEMORY.md for appending (zero bytes, nothing changed) and it was allowed, while .claude/agents/implementer.md, .claude/skills/tdd-cycle/SKILL.md and AGENTS.md were refused. .actuarii.json governs .claude/** and .mcp.json, but the denyWrite of .claude/settings.json has no entry for them, and neither does the one the installer writes into a target: both drop them through SELF_PROTECTED = (".claude/**", ".mcp.json"), on the belief that Claude Code's sandbox protects them by itself. It protects only some of .claude (its settings, agents, skills, hooks), not a directory a project adds there, such as the governed memory .claude/memory/. AGENTS 7.3 says every governed path MUST have its denyWrite entry, and tests/security/test_sandbox_settings.py pins the exemption instead of the rule (SELF_PROTECTED, test_the_configuration_read_lists_the_two_paths_the_sandbox_protects_by_itself).
decisions: D1 No exemption: every entry of governed_paths gets its denyWrite entry, in .claude/settings.json and in what the installer writes into a target. `.claude/**` gives "./.claude" and `.mcp.json` gives "./.mcp.json", by the existing rule ("./" plus the path without its trailing /**). SELF_PROTECTED goes, from tools/install.py and from the test.
D2 .claude/settings.json: denyWrite gains "./.claude" and "./.mcp.json"; nothing else in the file changes (permissions, hooks, includeGitInstructions, the other sandbox values and keys).

D3 tools/install.py: deny_write_entries() derives its entries from every governed path of EXAMPLE_CONFIG. The merge into a target's existing denyWrite stays as today: existing entries kept and first, the kit's appended when missing; a second run changes nothing (I3).

D4 tests/security/test_sandbox_settings.py: expected_deny_write derives from every governed path; test_deny_entries_are_dot_slash_paths_without_the_trailing_glob expects ./.claude and ./.mcp.json too; test_the_configuration_read_lists_the_two_paths_the_sandbox_protects_by_itself is replaced by a test of the rule of AGENTS 7.3: every governed path of the committed configuration has its entry in the committed denyWrite. It is a change of the specification (the exemption was wrong), not a test changed to hide a failure (AGENTS 8.2).
D5 tests/unit/test_installer.py imports expected_deny_write from the settings test, so its expectations follow D4; change it only where an assertion still encodes the exemption.

D6 A probe of the real sandbox cannot run in the suite: pytest does not run under Claude Code's sandbox in the CI. The guarantee is checked as configuration here; the executing agent probes it in the next session, where the changed settings apply.
D7 .claude/settings.json does not apply to the running session (tools/hooks/block_config_changes.py): nothing has to be restarted during the task.

D8 The session's validator requires a Rationale in every proposal (AGENTS.md 2.2). The schema of validate_proposal shown in this session may be an older copy without it: include it anyway, or the proposal comes back INVALID_JSON.

D9 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, `pytest tests/` exits 0 at the commit; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.

behaviours.statement: The committed denyWrite holds an entry for every governed path of .actuarii.json, ./.claude and ./.mcp.json included, plus the configuration file and the audit database, and nothing else.
The installer writes into a fresh target a denyWrite with an entry for every governed path of its example configuration, ./.claude and ./.mcp.json included.
A target's existing denyWrite keeps its entries, first and in order, and gains only the missing kit entries; a second run changes nothing.
Everything else the sandbox tests pin holds as today: the strict values, the set of keys, a dropped, extra or duplicated entry is a problem.

tests.must_catch: a committed denyWrite that lacks the entry of a governed path, .claude/** or .mcp.json included, or a test that exempts a governed path
tests.reason: at base ./.claude and ./.mcp.json are not in the committed denyWrite, and the test exempts them

tests.must_catch: an installer that writes a denyWrite without ./.claude or ./.mcp.json
tests.reason: at base deny_write_entries drops them through SELF_PROTECTED

tests.must_catch: a change to the strict sandbox values, its keys, the configuration and audit database entries, the merge with an existing denyWrite, or idempotence
tests.reason: these hold at base and must keep holding

commit_message: fix(sandbox): cada ruta gobernada con su denyWrite, sin eximir .claude ni .mcp.json
